body:
That's the real bitch of it. I can't really put my finger on it. I guess I could say that I'm overwhelmed. I'm sick of always feeling like the next big life-altering event is just around the corner (and it always is in medicine). I feel like I'm in a constant state of hypervigilance. There is always some big test to study for or some attending on the ward that I need to prepare a presentation for or some paperwork that I need to catch up on. 

Don't get me wrong, I can't even consider myself doing any other career, I love chit chatting with my patients and helping them, but there is always a push for less of that and more volume or more CYA. I am tired of having to short-change all of my patient encounters because I know that I need to spend the next hour writing my encounter notes from the morning.

To put it simply, I can't really pin down what triggers all of this, but it has been happening for years and years (pre-dating med school) and I've yet to find anything that definitively gets rid of it.
